description: Committee recommended approving Option A for improved accessibility.
This includes rail signalization coordination at the intersection.

chips.text: Recommended
A councillor stated, "we don't compromise on safety" regarding intersection improvements.
53 commercial tenants along Miller Avenue supported Option A.
Administration recommended Option C, while the committee recommended Option A.
The level of service for alternative routes in Option C was not assessed.
Citizen advocate urged for Option C, citing safety over business convenience.
Several councillors opposed Option A, arguing it would not adequately improve vehicle safety.
Injurious affection claims due to devalued properties were a concern for Option C.

speakers.name: Jarvis Rein
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Millar Ave
said: Supports Option A for pedestrian safety, minimal traffic pattern change.
Option C significantly harms businesses, doubles project cost.
Option C's accident reduction is negligible (0.001%).

speakers.name: John Kearley
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 51st St and Millar Ave_redact
said: Supports Option A for pedestrian safety and multi-use pathway.
Option A improves active transportation without impacting access.
Commends committee's compromise, encourages council to vote for Option A.

speakers.name: Jason Hanson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 51st and Millar Intersection Improvement
said: Option A fails to address dangerous gridlock at 51st/Miller.
Businesses prioritize profit over safety, ignoring real dangers.
Council should support Option C for improved safety, not Option A.

description: Recommends 3.0-meter shared pathway on Millar Avenue's east side.
Also recommends 43rd Street north side pathway, south side sidewalk.

chips.text: Recommended
Jason Hansen used a Jurassic Park analogy to criticize the watered-down safety proposals.
Businesses along Millar Avenue were concerned about parking, access, and traffic flow impacts.
Transit ridership numbers for the route were not available during the discussion.
Businesses generally supported the one-sided pathway as a reasonable compromise.
Transit users and pedestrians face safety risks, especially in winter, with only one-sided pathways.

speakers.name: Jarvis Rein
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Millar Ave
said: Glad committee reached reasonable compromise for one-sided path.
Single use pathway works well on Warman Road, will work on Miller.
Construction will cause minor blips, but not a major problem.

speakers.name: John Kearley
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 51st St and Millar Ave_redact
said: Supports transportation committee's recommendations as a viable compromise.
Increases pedestrian and cycling access, benefiting the area.
Sharing access is caring; provides mobility opportunities for all.

speakers.name: Keith Moen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Connecting Millar Avenue from 43rd Street to Marquis Drive - Redacted
said: Supports committee's recommendation for a 3-meter shared pathway on east side.
Original design was too extensive, raised concerns about access, parking, traffic.
Compromise balances pedestrian safety with operational needs of businesses.

speakers.name: Jason Hanson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Connecting Millar from 43rd to Marquis
said: Business community scuttled well-engineered proposals for watered-down options.
Safety concerns don't matter to businesses if it impacts parking.
Vote for original option with shared pathways on both sides.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Connecting Millar Avenue
said: Supports administration's recommendation for pathways on both sides.
One-sided sidewalk forces southbound bus riders to risk lives crossing.
Approving half a concept plan is illogical; approve full plan for future.

speakers.name: Sam Robarts
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Connecting Millar Avenue from 43rd to Marquis
said: Original design would cause loss of parking, affecting business operations.
Committee's one-sided pathway recommendation balances needs of stakeholders.
Eliminating paved parking would reduce property value and lease competitiveness.

speakers.name: Clark Barzeele
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Millar Avenue Pathways Project
said: Thanks traffic committee for reasonable compromise option.
Original proposal would negatively affect business by 25%, impacting jobs.
Pathway project is important for team members using bus, walking, biking.

speakers.name: Zain Abidin
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Millar Avenue Transportation Projects
said: Supports original option 1B with mixed-use pathways on both sides.
Unfortunate to drop to one side; causes difficulties for pedestrians.
City's well-thought-out proposal was derailed by committee motion.
